newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Trade union strikes in support of Swaziland.
newsitem.headline: Trade union strikes in support of Swaziland.

text.p: South Africa's largest trade union Cosatu said on Thursday it planned a day of action in support of strikers in Swaziland.

The Congress of South African Trade Unions said it would refuse to handle goods to and from Swaziland on an unspecified future date. It said members in regions bordering Swaziland would hold demonstrations at the frontier.

A national strike was called 10 days ago by the Swaziland Federation of Trade Unions seeking democratic change in the tiny mountain kingdom. A 1973 royal decree vested all state powers in the monarch and banned political activity.
The sugar and timber industries, Swaziland's biggest foreign exchange earners, have been hardest hit.
Swazi unions are also demanding the release of four union leaders arrested at the beginning of the strike and charged with violating public order. They will appear in a Swazi court next Wednesday.
